text:
devops-bot: ALERT: prod-us-west: GPU pool 'v2-large' admission > 95% and API 503 rate increased by 18% in last 2m

maria (eng-fleet): seeing big queue depth on inference-proxy, admission controller started rejecting at 90% capacity, lots of short-lived retries. rolling errors from edge -> 503s.

sam (oncall): oncall joining, which regions affected?

maria (eng-fleet): primarily prod-us-west, small spillover to prod-us-east from routing fallback. We also saw a sudden surge of short-seq requests from one customer namespace (acct-314).

ingrid (sre): logs show admission_counter.increment() spike coincident with a mass re-run job from acct-314. KV cache misses also spiked.

kevin (infra): infra metrics: GPU utilization for v2-large jumped from 60% -> 98% in ~3m. Autoscaler didn't add nodes because pool cap was hit (pool max=40). Admission controller configured to aim for 90% steady-state, but throttle policy not tuned for bursty workloads.

liz (product): is this related to the new batch-inference rollout? We pushed a customer feature yesterday.

maria (eng-fleet): not the rollout itself, looks like a user-triggered batch replay. acct-314 ran many parallel calls with long contexts; KV cache thrash and continuous batching collapsed throughput.

sam (oncall): mitigation plan executed: 1) enable cross-region fallback for low-tier requests (prod-east) 2) temporarily increase pool max to 60 (hotpatch) 3) apply rate-limit on acct-314. Any objections? :thumbsup:

kevin (infra): +1 to emergency scale, already started node spin-up (aws-spot->ondemand fallback). ETA for nodes ~ 4m.

maria (eng-fleet): applied acct-314 rate-limit via per-namespace quota rule. Reduced new admission by ~70%.

ingrid (sre): after scale and quota, 503s decreased to baseline in ~6m. Need follow-ups: autoscaler thresholds, admission backoff policy, and circuit-breaker for noisy namespaces.

liz (product): can we notify the customer? They likely hit this accidentally. I'll draft outreach.

kevin (infra): note: cost spike from spot->ondemand fallback will be ~+18% for the hour. Finance FYI.

maria (eng-fleet): collecting traces and p95/p99 latency distributions. Key observation: continuous batching logic aggregated many parallel short requests into huge batches because of long context sizes, causing GPU memory pressure and KV cache eviction storms.

sam (oncall): quick tl;dr to put in postmortem: surge from acct-314 triggered batching+cache thrash -> pools hit cap -> admission controller started rejecting -> fallback routing overloaded secondary regions -> cascading 503s.

ingrid (sre): agree. I'll start the postmortem doc and capture timeline. Immediate actions (done): rate-limited offending namespace, added cross-region fallback backpressure limit, temporarily increased pool limit. Next actions (owner):
- maria: add per-namespace circuit breaker and explicit batching caps (owner: maria (eng-fleet))
- kevin: adjust autoscaler to consider queue depth + GPU mem pressure (owner: kevin (infra))
- ingrid: write incident postmortem + RCA and runbook updates (owner: ingrid (sre))
- product: outreach to acct-314 and confirm intent (owner: liz (product))

maria (eng-fleet): will also add heuristics to avoid bundling short-seq low-cost requests into large batches.

liz (product): noted, will start customer reach-out now.

sam (oncall): OK closing the critical pager. If anyone sees re-escalation, re-open. Thanks all for fast responses. :raised_hands:

monitoring-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: prod-us-west incident resolved at 2026-03-18T14:17:40Z (see go/ops/incidents/1770023456 for draft postmortem)

ingrid (sre): draft summary for postmortem: Root cause: unbounded customer-driven batch replay that bypassed expected client-side rate limits and produced extreme batching and KV cache thrash; contributing factors: autoscaler pool cap, admission controller config not tuned for high burstiness, lack of per-namespace circuit breakers.

maria (eng-fleet): additional note: recommend a short-term safety knob that rejects batch requests above an absolute token size threshold to protect memory.

kevin (infra): filing infra ticket to relax pool hard cap and add autoscaler scaling-factor for mem pressure: infra/1781.

ingrid (sre): adding postmortem owners and timeline. I'll ping for reviews when draft is ready.

liz (product): +1 on outreach draft, will loop in acct-314 success manager.

sam (oncall): great job. Closing thread, will link to final postmortem when published.
